findings.name: Hacker News Firebase API (topstories/newstories/beststories)
findings.http_status: 200 (verified: topstories 4501B, newstories 4501B, item/1.json 200, maxitem returns int)
findings.notes: Returns arrays of numeric item IDs; /item/{id}.json gives id, time (unix), title, url, score, descendants, kids. /maxitem + polling new stories gives clean 'new since yesterday' dedupe. No HTML needed.
findings.reliability: High / stable (no auth, no bot wall)

findings.name: Hacker News Algolia Search API
findings.http_status: 200 (verified, application/json; search_by_date, front_page, comment tags all return hits)
findings.rate_limit: Unofficial soft cap (~10k req/hr); be polite
findings.notes: Each hit has objectID, created_at, created_at_i (unix), points, num_comments, title, url, story_id. numericFilters=created_at_i>UNIX gives exactly 'new since yesterday'. Best dedupe-ready HN source. Full-text search supported.

findings.name: Hacker News front-page RSS
findings.notes: RSS of current front page (guid/pubDate). Simpler than Algolia but no filtering by time/score; use only as fallback.

findings.name: Reddit JSON API (per-subreddit)
findings.auth: None works but IP bot-walled; reliable use requires OAuth (free app registration)
findings.http_status: 403 (verified, text/html bot-wall — all UAs incl. custom UA and curl/8.0 blocked)
findings.rate_limit: OAuth free tier: 100 queries/min per OAuth client
findings.notes: Fragile from datacenter IPs. Official path is OAuth (oauth.reddit.com), which returned 403 without a token. Reddit's Responsible Builder Policy closed self-service app registration (manual approval); commercial use $0.24 per 1k calls. Use the .rss feed or plan for OAuth approval.
findings.reliability: Fragile (bot wall) / paid for reliable scale

findings.name: Reddit Atom RSS (per-subreddit)
findings.http_status: 200 (verified 27688B, application/atom+xml; 25 entries, id=t3_xxxxx, published+updated ISO timestamps)
findings.rate_limit: Undocumented but AGGRESSIVE per-IP: 429 after ~2 rapid requests; needs ~10s spacing (confirmed)
findings.notes: Only free no-auth Reddit option that currently returns data. Atom entries carry t3_<id> and published/updated for dedupe. Throttle hard (>=10s per sub, stagger across subs), or prefer OAuth.

findings.name: GitHub Security Advisories (GHSA) API
findings.notes: Fields: ghsa_id, cve_id, published_at, updated_at, severity, summary, vulnerabilities[]. Filter by published/updated since for new-since-yesterday. Same host backs GHSA Database. Gold standard for ecosystem advisories.

findings.name: GitHub Advisory Database (repo contents / raw git)
findings.rate_limit: GitHub 60/hr unauth, 5000/hr auth; git clone avoids API limits
findings.notes: OSV-format JSON (id, modified, published, affected) per advisory. git clone once + git pull is the efficient bulk path.

findings.name: OSV.dev API (query / querybatch / vulns)
findings.notes: Aggregates GHSA/CVE/ecosystem advisories. Returns id + modified (ISO) for dedupe, summary, affected ranges. querybatch for many packages at once. No 'list recent' endpoint — poll per-package or use ecosystem zips.

findings.name: OSV ecosystem bulk export (zips)
findings.notes: Complete per-ecosystem OSV records; heavy download but comprehensive and dedupe-friendly (each record has id+modified). Not available for 'GHSA' key.

findings.name: NVD CVE API 2.0
findings.auth: None, or free API key (email request) for higher limit
findings.rate_limit: 5 requests / rolling 30s WITHOUT key; 50 requests / rolling 30s WITH free key
findings.notes: Authoritative CVE metadata (id, published, lastModified, CVSS, references). Use pubStartDate+pubEndDate windows for new-since-yesterday. Slow/paginated — sleep between calls as NIST recommends.
findings.reliability: High but slow; rate-limited without key

findings.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog
findings.notes: Single JSON with catalogVersion, dateReleased, vulnerabilities[] (cveID, dateAdded, vendorProject, shortDescription). Updated ~daily; dateAdded enables dedupe. Highest-signal vuln source (actively exploited only).

findings.name: CVE.org / CVE Services API (cvelistV5)
findings.notes: Authoritative CVE record per ID (cveMetadata state/datePublished, containers). No bulk 'recent' query — pair with NVD for listing; bulk via cvelistV5 git repo.

findings.name: dev.to (Forem) API
findings.auth: None for reads (API key only for posting)
findings.notes: Fields: id, published_at, title, url, tag_list, positive_reactions_count, comments_count, description. ?tag=ai and ?top=1 filter by topic/period; published_at gives dedupe. Note: 'latest' feed can contain spam — prefer tag+top.

findings.name: Anthropic News / Changelog
findings.notes: NO official RSS. Must HTML-scrape (Next.js data/hydration payload) or use a third-party proxy/generator. Fragile for automation.

findings.name: OpenAI News RSS
findings.http_status: 200 (724821B, text/xml; verified via redirect). Note: openai.com/news/ page itself = 403 to bots
findings.notes: Valid RSS 2.0 with items (title, link, guid, pubDate). Use the RSS, not the HTML page (bot-walled).
findings.reliability: High via RSS; page scraping blocked

findings.name: Google DeepMind News RSS
findings.notes: RSS with pubDate/guid. Page path /discover/blog/ 301s; use the rss.xml directly.

findings.name: Google AI (blog.google) RSS
findings.notes: Google's AI product news RSS; publish dates in items.

findings.name: Google Developers Blog RSS

findings.notes: Blogger-backed RSS for Google dev platform news.

findings.name: Google Online Security Blog RSS
findings.notes: Google's security advisories/research. Must add ?alt=rss (bare /feeds/posts/default 302s).

findings.name: Google Project Zero feed
findings.notes: Very large (full post bodies). Use conditional GET (ETag/If-Modified-Since) to avoid re-downloading 13MB daily.

findings.name: Meta Engineering Blog RSS

findings.name: Lobsters

findings.name: Stack Overflow Blog RSS

findings.name: Changelog
findings.category: a) dev news / c) AI tooling

findings.name: arXiv RSS (category updates)
findings.rate_limit: RSS endpoint no documented hard limit; be polite
findings.notes: Daily new-submission digests per category. Announcement cadence (weekdays). Use RSS instead of the API which rate-limits hard.

findings.name: arXiv API (query)
findings.http_status: 429 (verified 'Rate exceeded.' from shared IP; endpoint exists and is Atom)
findings.rate_limit: Officially ~1 request / 3 seconds; frequently 429s on shared/datacenter IPs
findings.notes: Powerful (search, sortBy=submittedDate) but unreliable from cloud IPs. Prefer the per-category RSS feed for a daily digest.

findings.name: GitHub Trending
findings.notes: NO official API or RSS. Requires HTML scraping (no stable IDs/timestamps). Substitute with the GitHub Search API below, which is machine-readable.

findings.name: GitHub Repo Search API (trending substitute)
findings.rate_limit: Search API: 10 req/min unauthenticated, 30 req/min authenticated
findings.notes: Machine-readable 'trending new repos' with id, full_name, created_at, stargazers_count, description — no scraping, dedupe-ready.

findings.name: npm registry search + downloads
findings.rate_limit: None documented (be polite); downloads API CORS-enabled
findings.notes: Package metadata + weekly download counts for trend signals. No auth, stable.

findings.name: TLDR (tech/AI) newsletter RSS
findings.notes: Daily-curated dev & AI newsletter items with links+pubDate. Excellent signal-to-noise for a daily digest.

findings.auth: OAuth 2.0 app + PAID tier (Basic ~$200/mo historically; newer pay-per-use credits); no usable free read tier
findings.notes: Not free — read access requires a paid plan; recent-search heavily capped. Do not include unless budgeted; use HN/Reddit/Lobsters for dev chatter instead.

fragile_or_paid: Reddit JSON API — 403 bot wall from datacenter IPs; reliable access needs OAuth (free tier 100 QPM but self-service app registration closed; commercial $0.24/1k calls).
Reddit Atom .rss — works without auth but hard per-IP rate limit (429 after ~2 rapid requests; needs ~10s spacing).
Anthropic News — no RSS (/news/rss.xml and /rss.xml both 404); HTML scrape/headless required.
Meta AI Blog (ai.meta.com) — returns HTTP 400 (blocked/geofenced); no working RSS.
Ben's Bites — no public RSS (beehiiv feed 404); scrape/headless required.
The Batch (deeplearning.ai) — all feed paths 404/308; no reachable RSS.
Uber Engineering feed — 406 Not Acceptable / 404; edge-blocked.
arXiv API query endpoint — 429 'Rate exceeded' from shared/cloud IPs; use category RSS instead.
GDELT DOC API — enforced 1 request / 5 seconds (429 otherwise).
GitHub Trending — HTML only, no API/RSS, no stable IDs/timestamps; use GitHub Search API instead.
X/Twitter API — paid only (no usable free read tier).
recommended_shortlist: Hacker News Algolia API (numericFilters=created_at_i>UNIX) — dedupe-ready, highest dev signal
Hacker News Firebase API (newstories + /item/{id}) — clean incremental IDs
GitHub Security Advisories (GHSA) API — phrased advisories with published_at/updated_at
OSV.dev API (querybatch) — cross-ecosystem vulns by package, id+modified
CISA KEV catalog JSON — only actively-exploited CVEs, dateAdded for dedupe
NVD CVE API 2.0 (register free key) — authoritative CVE metadata, date-windowed
dev.to API (tag=ai, top=1) — free, JSON, published_at dedupe
TLDR RSS (tldr.tech/api/rss/tech + /ai) — curated dev+AI, high signal-to-noise
arXiv RSS cs.AI/cs.SE/cs.LG — daily AI/SE research digests
Simon Willison's Weblog Atom — top AI-for-devs practitioner blog
OpenAI News RSS + Google DeepMind RSS — vendor AI announcements
Cloudflare / GitHub / Netflix engineering RSS — vendor eng depth
unverified: X/Twitter API v2 — endpoint not exercised (requires paid credentials); pricing/limits taken from secondary sources.
Reddit OAuth-authenticated endpoint (oauth.reddit.com) — 403 without a token; 100 QPM free-tier limit taken from secondary sources.
Anthropic HTML scrape feasibility — page returns 200 but item IDs/timestamps not verified without a scraper.
Meta AI blog alternate hosts — only ai.meta.com/blog/rss/ tested; no alternative feed confirmed.
